drafted_from: tool:make-a-contact-sheet-of-pictures-or-video-frames row in tool-rows.json, do-work/make_contact_sheet.py and test/test_make_contact_sheet.py
start_here: Say to your AI: "Lay out the four cake photos in pictures/ as one contact sheet, three to a row, each 300 pixels wide with its name under it, and save it as sheet.jpg." It writes a request file, runs make_contact_sheet.py on your computer and tells you the sheet it made.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads one JSON request file and writes sheet pictures, keeping nothing between runs.
instructions: 1. Install what it needs once: clone the Workshop repository, run python3 -m pip install -U pillow, and brew install ffmpeg only if you want a sheet of video frames.
2. Say what you want laid out; your AI reads the row with tools:list and writes a JSON request file with kind (pictures, frames-at-times or frames-at-a-rate), out and the fields that kind takes.
3. It runs `python3 tools/make-a-contact-sheet-of-pictures-or-video-frames/do-work/make_contact_sheet.py request.json` from the Workshop checkout and reads the last line.

4. {"result": {"sheets": [...], "tiles": n}} names the sheet files and how many pictures or frames are on them; {"error": "..."} says what to change in the request. Open the sheet to choose or check by eye.

worked_examples.title: Four photos in a grid of three, names below
worked_examples.ask: Make a contact sheet of my four cake photos, three to a row.
worked_examples.given: From tools/make-a-contact-sheet-of-pictures-or-video-frames/test/test_make_contact_sheet.py (test_grid_size_and_cells_with_label_below): the AI reads the row, then runs `python3 tools/make-a-contact-sheet-of-pictures-or-video-frames/do-work/make_contact_sheet.py request.json` where request.json is {"kind": "pictures", "out": "sheet.jpg", "columns": 3, "cell_width": 300, "pictures": [{"path": "pictures/cake0.png", "label": "n0"}, {"path": "pictures/cake1.png", "label": "n1"}, {"path": "pictures/cake2.png", "label": "n2"}, {"path": "pictures/cake3.png", "label": "n3"}]}; the pictures are 800x450, 600x800, 800x300 and 640x360.
worked_examples.hands_back: The last line printed is {"result": {"sheets": ["sheet.jpg"], "tiles": 4}}. The sheet is 924 pixels wide and 394 tall: three cells of 300 plus 6 padding each, two rows of 168 picture height plus a 14 pixel label strip plus 12, plus 6; the 600x800 picture is cut to its middle so it fills its cell. With an empty pictures list the last line is {"error": "... at least one picture ..."} and the exit status is 1.
